record.title: The weak covariance-matrix conjecture for planar leaf-rooted trees
record.statement:
Let $G$ and $G'$ be planar leaf-rooted trees with no vertices of degree $2$. For each tree, let $\mathbf{\Sigma}_G$ and $\mathbf{\Sigma}_{G'}$ be the covariance matrices determined by the large-$t$ behavior of the winding statistic of the two-particle exclusion process on $\binom{G}{2}$ and $\binom{G'}{2}$, respectively, where $\binom{G}{2}$ is the graph of unordered pairs of distinct vertices of $G$ joined when one particle moves along an edge while the other remains fixed. **The Weak Conjecture.** If

$$
\mathbf{\Sigma}_G=\mathbf{\Sigma}_{G'},
$$

then $G$ and $G'$ have the same degree sequence. This weaker claim would still show that the winding covariance contains nontrivial information about the combinatorics of the underlying tree. The paper presents it as an open consequence that would be significant for graph configuration spaces.

record.title: The tiling characterization of 4-colorable maximal planar graphs
record.statement:
A **maximal planar graph** is a planar graph to which no edge can be added while preserving planarity. The **every-zero graphic group** $\{F_{\textrm{inner}\bigtriangleup};\oplus\}$ is the group shown in Figure 4(c), whose elements are the relevant graphic objects under the operation $\oplus$. A graph is **tiled by** this group when it is obtained by the tiling construction described for the planar graphic lattice. **Tiling characterization.** A maximal planar graph is 4-colorable if and only if it can be tiled by the every-zero graphic group

$$
\{F_{\textrm{inner}\bigtriangleup};\oplus\}.
$$

This gives a proposed structural characterization of 4-colorability for maximal planar graphs in terms of the paper's graphic-lattice construction. The source presents the claim without evidence of resolution; its status is therefore left open.

record.title: The crabbed-path strengthening for cocircuit distances
record.statement:
Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{M}}$ be a uniform oriented matroid, and let $X,Y\in\operatorname{\mathcal{C}}^*(\operatorname{\mathcal{M}})$ be cocircuits. Let $S(X,Y)$ denote the set used to define crabbed paths, and suppose $S(X,Y)=\emptyset$. A path is **crabbed** from $X$ to $Y$ when it satisfies the corresponding sign-coordinate restriction throughout.

**Crabbed-path conjecture.** There exists a crabbed path from $X$ to $Y$ whose length is no bigger than the length of any path from $X$ to $Y$ in $\operatorname{\mathcal{M}}$.

This is presented as a strengthening of the London–Paris conjecture. The surrounding discussion explains that the related tope-path conjecture would imply a quadratic bound on polytope diameters, while the linear diameter conjecture is already refuted; the crabbed-path strengthening itself is not resolved in the paper.
record.source_name: Ilan Adler, Jesús A. De Loera, Steven Klee and Zhenyang Zhang, “Diameters of Cocircuit Graphs of Oriented Matroids: An Update”, arXiv:2006.08922 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.08922

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2020). “Then $\diam(G^*(\mathcal{M})) \leq n-r+2.$ Conjecture bears a striking resemblance to the famous Hirsch conjecture for convex polytopes, which was disproved by Santos , and with good reason.”

record.title: The new version of Gordon's identities
record.statement:
Let $r\geq 2$ and $1\leq i\leq r$. For a partition $\Lambda=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m)$, define its $(i,\ell)$-new parts recursively by

$$
p_{i,\ell}(\Lambda)=\begin{cases}\lambda_m&\text{if }\ell=1,\\lambda_{m-\sum_{j=1}^{\ell-1}p_{i,j}(\Lambda)}&\text{if }2\leq\ell\leq i,\\lambda_{m+\ell-i-\sum_{j=1}^{\ell-1}p_{i,j}(\Lambda)}&\text{if }i<\ell\leq r-1,\end{cases}
$$

where $\lambda_j=0$ for $j\leq 0$, and if $p_{i,\ell}(\Lambda)=0$, then $p_{i,j}(\Lambda)=0$ for $j>\ell$. Let $N_i(\Lambda)$ be the number of nonzero $(i,\ell)$-new parts. **The new version of Gordon's identities.** For an integer $n$, let $C_{r,i}(n)$ denote the number of partitions $\Lambda=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_s)$ of $n$ with at most $i-1$ parts equal to $1$ and either $N_i(\Lambda)<r-1$, or $N_i(\Lambda)=r-1$ and

$$
s\leq\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}p_{i,j}(\Lambda)-(r-i).
$$

Then $C_{r,i}(n)=B_{r,i}(n)=A_{r,i}(n)$, where $B_{r,i}(n)$ and $A_{r,i}(n)$ are the quantities in Gordon's identities. This conjecture proposes a new partition-theoretic realization of Gordon's identities; the source presents it as a conjectural consequence of the proposed leading monomial ideals, and no resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Pooneh Afsharijoo, “Looking for a new member of Gordon's identities”, arXiv:2006.09216 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.09216

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2020).

record.title: Inequivalence conjecture for higher-dimensional halfspace and projection closures
record.statement:
Let $k\geq 3$ and $n\geq k$. For a rational polyhedron $P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$, let $\mathcal{H}_k(P)$ be its $k$-halfspace closure, and let

$$
\mathcal{P}_k(P):=\bigcap_{L\in\mathcal{L}_k}\bigl(P_{I,L}+L^\perp\bigr),
$$

where $\mathcal{L}_k$ is the family of $k$-dimensional subspaces, $P_{I,L}$ is the integer hull in the corresponding projection, and $L^\perp$ is the orthogonal complement of $L$. **Inequivalence conjecture.** For any fixed natural number $k\geq 3$, and any $n\geq k$, there are instances of rational polyhedra $P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ such that

$$
\mathcal{H}_k(P)\neq\mathcal{P}_k(P).
$$

The claim is motivated by the failure in dimensions three and higher of representing integer hulls as intersections of corner polyhedra; the source notes that it is true when $n=k$, but gives no general resolution for the stated range.
record.source_name: Amitabh Basu and Hongyi Jiang, “Two-halfspace closure”, arXiv:2006.11587 (2021).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.11587

record.title: Conjecture on the parameters and weight distribution of codes from almost bent exponents
record.statement:
Let $n=2m+1$, let $e$ be one of the almost bent exponents listed in the source's table, and choose $t$ with $\gcd(t,n)=1$. Define

$$
f(x)=(x^{2^t}+x)^e
$$

and let $\mathcal{C}_f$ be the associated linear code.

**Parameter and weight-distribution conjecture.** The parameters of $\mathcal{C}_f$ should be the same as those of the code in the cited theorem, namely the theorem's parameters for the corresponding construction; moreover, the weight distribution of $\mathcal{C}_f$ should be determined.

This conjecture is motivated by experimental results and extends the observed code-parameter phenomenon to the listed almost bent exponents. The supplied text does not include the referenced table or theorem, so the exact parameter tuple and the claimed weight distribution remain to be determined.

record.title: Signed $(p,q)$-enumerator identities for type B permutations
record.statement:
Let $B_n$ be the hyperoctahedral group of signed permutations, and for $sigma\in B_n$ let $\mathsf{fwex}(\sigma)$, $\mathsf{neg}(\sigma)$, $\mathsf{nest}_B(\sigma)$, and $\mathsf{cro}_B(\sigma)$ denote respectively the flag weak excedance, number of negative entries, type B nesting number, and type B crossing number. Let $R_{n}(t,p,q)$ be the $(p,q)$-derivative polynomial defined in the surrounding text. For $n\geq 1$, **the signed type B enumerator identities.**

$$
\sum_{\sigma\in B_n}(-1)^{\left\lfloor \frac{\mathsf{fwex}(\sigma)}{2}\right\rfloor}t^{\mathsf{neg}(\sigma)}p^{\mathsf{nest}_B(\sigma)}q^{\mathsf{cro}_B(\sigma)}=\begin{cases}(-1)^{\frac n2}(t+1)R_{n-1}(t,p,q)&\text{if $n$ is odd},\\(-1)^{\frac{n-1}{2}}(t-1)R_{n-1}(t,p,q)&\text{if $n$ is even},\end{cases}
$$

and

$$
\sum_{\sigma\in B_n}(-1)^{\left\lceil \frac{\mathsf{fwex}(\sigma)}{2}\right\rceil}t^{\mathsf{neg}(\sigma)}p^{\mathsf{nest}_B(\sigma)}q^{\mathsf{cro}_B(\sigma)}=\begin{cases}(-1)^{\frac n2}(t-1)R_{n-1}(t,p,q)&\text{if $n$ is even},\\(-1)^{\frac{n+1}{2}}(t+1)R_{n-1}(t,p,q)&\text{if $n$ is odd}.\end{cases}
$$

These identities give signed refinements of the joint crossing–nesting enumerator for type B permutations in terms of the $(p,q)$-derivative polynomials. The parser provides no resolution evidence, so the status is recorded as open.

record.title: Nonzero-coefficient conjecture for the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz framework
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal H$ be an $n$-uniform linear hypergraph with $n$ edges. For each pair of indices $1\leq i<k\leq n$, let $\Phi_{i,k}(\mathbf{x})$ be the polynomial defined from the chosen identifier spanning trees, and let a **Vandermonde-completable monomial** mean a monomial corresponding to an orientation whose base cliques can be oriented as transitive tournaments with every total in-degree at most $n-1$.

**Nonzero-coefficient conjecture.** One can choose the identifier spanning trees in a way that there is a Vandermonde-completable monomial with nonzero coefficient in

$$
\prod_{i<k}\Phi_{i,k}(\mathbf{x}).
$$

The conjecture is the missing algebraic step in the paper's approach to the Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture. The corresponding existence of Vandermonde-completable orientations is proved, but the required nonvanishing of the coefficient sum is left open.
record.source_name: Oliver Janzer and Zoltán Lóránt Nagy, “Coloring linear hypergraphs: the Erdős-Faber-Lovász conjecture and the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz”, arXiv:2007.00685 (2020).

record.title: Strong coefficientwise Hankel-total positivity conjecture for the GKP recurrence
record.statement:
Let $T(n,k)$ be defined by the shifted GKP recurrence

$$
T(n,k)=[\widetilde{\alpha}(n-1)+\widetilde{\beta}k+\widetilde{\gamma}]T(n-1,k)+[\widetilde{\alpha}'(n-1)+\widetilde{\beta}'(k-1)+\widetilde{\gamma}']T(n-1,k-1),
$$

and let $P_n(x;\widetilde{\bm{\mu}})$ be its row-generating polynomials, where $\widetilde{\bm{\mu}}=(\widetilde{\alpha},\widetilde{\beta},\widetilde{\gamma},\widetilde{\alpha}',\widetilde{\beta}',\widetilde{\gamma}')$. A sequence is **coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive** when every minor of its Hankel matrix has nonnegative coefficients in the indicated indeterminates.

**Strong coefficientwise Hankel-total positivity conjecture for the GKP recurrence.** The sequence

$$
\bm{P}=(P_n(x;\widetilde{\bm{\mu}}))_{n\geq 0}
$$

of row-generating polynomials of this shifted recurrence is coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive, jointly in the seven indeterminates $x,\widetilde{\alpha},\widetilde{\beta},\widetilde{\gamma},\widetilde{\alpha}',\widetilde{\beta}',\widetilde{\gamma}'$.

This is presented as a stronger version of the unshifted GKP positivity conjecture, obtained by an affine reparametrization, and remains unproved in the supplied text.

record.title: Family-size stabilization conjecture for complete multipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $n \geq 3$, let $1 \leq a_1 \leq \cdots \leq a_n$, and define

$$
e = \#E(K_{a_1, \ldots, a_{n-1}}).
$$

If $a_1 + \cdots + a_{n-1} > 6$ and $a_n \geq e$, then **the family-size stabilization conjecture** asserts that

$$
\left|\mathcal{F}(K_{a_1, \ldots, a_{n-1}, e-1})\right| = \left|\mathcal{F}(K_{a_1, \ldots, a_{n-1}, a_n})\right| - 1.
$$

Here $K_{a_1,\ldots,a_n}$ is the complete multipartite graph with part sizes $a_1,\ldots,a_n$, $\#E(G)$ denotes the number of edges of $G$, and $\mathcal{F}(G)$ denotes the family of graphs obtainable from $G$ by sequences of Triangle-Y and Y-Triangle moves. The conjecture predicts a precise one-unit difference between the family sizes at the indicated parameters, extending the pattern observed in the tables and the proved stabilization result for the related family-size function. The general assertion remains open in the source.
record.source_name: Danielle Gregg, Thomas W. Mattman, Zachary Porat and George Todd, “Family sizes for complete multipartite graphs”, arXiv:2008.12975 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.12975

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of August 2020).

record.title: Nonexistence of pairs of maximal frequency squares of half frequency
record.statement: A **frequency square** of type $(n;\lambda)$ is an $n\times n$ array in which each symbol occurs exactly $\lambda$ times in every row and every column. Two frequency squares are **orthogonal** if each ordered pair of symbols occurs equally often in corresponding cells. A set of $k$ mutually orthogonal frequency squares of type $(n;\lambda)$ is called $k$-MOFS$(n;\lambda)$, and it is **maximal** if no further frequency square of type $(n;\lambda)$ is orthogonal to every member of the set; such a set is denoted $k$-maxMOFS$(n;\lambda)$. **Nonexistence conjecture for pairs of maximal frequency squares.** If $n$ is even, then there does not exist a set of $2$-maxMOFS$(n;n/2)$. The conjecture is known when $4$ divides $n$, and it holds for $n<8$ by the stated nonexistence results. The case in which $n/2$ is odd remains open.
record.source_name: Nicholas J. Cavenagh, Adam Mammoliti and Ian M. Wanless, “Maximal sets of mutually orthogonal frequency squares”, arXiv:2009.03475 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.03475

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2020).

record.title: Conciseness conjecture for commutators of non-commutator words
record.statement:
Let $w=w(x_1,\dots,x_k)$ be a group-word, and let $G_w$ denote the set of all values of $w$ in a group $G$. The verbal subgroup $w(G)$ is the subgroup generated by $G_w$, and $w$ is **concise** if $w(G)$ is finite whenever $G_w$ is finite. Let $u_1,\dots,u_s$ be non-commutator words, with the variables in the different words disjoint as assumed for commutator words in the paper. **Conciseness conjecture.** The word

$$
[u_1,\dots,u_s]
$$

is concise whenever the words $u_1,\dots,u_s$ are non-commutator. This conjecture is a refinement of P. Hall's disproved conjecture that every word is concise; it is motivated by known conciseness results for non-commutator words, multilinear commutator words, Engel words in small weights, and commutators of two non-commutator words. The source presents this as a natural conjecture, and no resolution of this specific statement is given.
record.source_name: João Azevedo and Pavel Shumyatsky, “On finiteness of verbal subgroups”, arXiv:2009.10121 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.10121

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of September 2020). “P. Hall had conjectured that every word is concise but the conjecture was refuted by Ivanov in .”

record.title: Polytope characterization of induced subgraphs with nonzero Euler characteristic
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with no induced cycles of length divisible by three. An **induced subgraph** is a subgraph obtained by taking a vertex set of $G$ and all edges between those vertices. A polytope is the convex hull of finitely many points in a Euclidean space, and its reduced Euler characteristic is denoted by $\tilde{\chi}$.

**Polytope characterization conjecture.** There is a polytope $P$ whose vertices are labelled by the edges of $G$ and whose faces are in bijection with the induced subgraphs of $G$ having reduced Euler characteristic $\pm1$. That is, the vertices of a face of $P$ correspond to the edges of an induced subgraph of $G$.

The source presents this as a conjectural connection with edge polytopes. It gives the complete-bipartite graph example as motivation, but does not state a resolution of the general claim.
record.source_name: Alexander Engstrom, “On the topological Kalai-Meshulam conjecture”, arXiv:2009.11077 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.11077

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of September 2020).

record.title: Conjecture on valid orientations with four exceptional boundary vertices
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a plane graph with a valid prescription function $p:V(G)\rightarrow\{-1,0,1\}$, a specified face $F_G$, and at most four specified vertices $d,r,s,t$. The vertex $d$, when present, is a degree-$3$ boundary vertex that may be oriented; each of $r,s,t$, when present, is a degree-$3$ boundary vertex. Assume

$$
G\text{ is 3-edge-connected,}
$$

$G$ has at most four $3$-edge-cuts, only $\delta(\{d\})$, $\delta(\{r\})$, $\delta(\{s\})$, or $\delta(\{t\})$, and every vertex outside the boundary of $F_G$ has five edge-disjoint paths to that boundary.

**Conjecture on valid orientations with four exceptional boundary vertices.** Then $G$ has a valid orientation.

This conjecture extends the paper's orientation theorem by allowing further degree-$3$ boundary vertices and is presented as best possible in view of related counterexamples.
record.source_name: Jamie V. de Jong, “Two Strong 3-Flow Theorems for Planar Graphs”, arXiv:2011.02140 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.02140

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2020). “This is known as the $3$-Flow Conjecture, and while progress has been made for many classes of graphs, it is still an open problem.”

record.title: Conjecture on valid orientations for two specified faces
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a plane graph with a valid prescription function $p:V(G)\rightarrow\{-1,0,1\}$, two specified faces $F_G$ and $F_G^*$, and at most one specified vertex $d$ or $t$. If $d$ is present, it is an oriented vertex of degree $3$, $4$, or $5$ on the boundary of one of the specified faces. If $t$ is present, it is a degree-$3$ vertex on the boundary of one of them. Assume

$$
G\text{ is 3-edge-connected,}
$$

$G$ has at most one $3$-edge-cut, only $\delta(\{d\})$ or $\delta(\{t\})$, and every vertex outside the boundaries of $F_G$ and $F_G^*$ has five edge-disjoint paths to their union.

**Conjecture on valid orientations for two specified faces.** Then $G$ has a valid orientation.

This removes from the preceding theorem the requirement that the oriented vertex lie on both specified faces and the requirement that the faces have a common vertex. The source presents the assertion as an open extension.

record.title: Carnevale–Voll's factorisation conjecture for multiset Euler–Mahonian polynomials
record.statement:
Let $\eta$ be a composition, and let $S_{\eta}$ denote the associated multiset permutations. For a polynomial $f\in\mathbb{Z}[x,y]$, call it **unitary** if there are $F\in\mathbb{Z}[Y]$ and $a,b\in\mathbb{N}_0$ such that $f(x,y)=F(x^ay^b)$ and every complex root of $F$ has absolute value $1$.

**Carnevale–Voll's factorisation conjecture.** The polynomial giving the joint distribution of $(\operatorname{den},\operatorname{exc})$ over $S_{\eta}$ has a unitary factor if and only if $\eta=(m^r)$ is a rectangle with $r$ even and $m$ odd. In that case,

$$
\sum_{w\in S_{\eta}}x^{\operatorname{den}(w)}y^{\operatorname{exc}(w)}=\left(1+x^{\frac{rm}{2}}y\right)f^{\eta}_0(x,y),
$$

where $f^{\eta}_0(x,y)$ has no unitary factor.

This is a reformulation of the factorisation conjecture for joint $(\operatorname{des},\operatorname{maj})$ distributions over multiset permutations. The stated factorisation singles out the unitary factor $1+x^{rm/2}y$ in exactly the even-by-odd rectangular cases; its resolution is not given in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Angela Carnevale and Elena Tielker, “On Denert's statistic”, arXiv:2108.04700 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.04700

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2021).

record.title: The quadric-configuration conjecture for double $2d$ configurations
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth extremal surface of degree $d$, and let a **double $2d$** on $X$ be a pair of sets of $2d$ lines satisfying the incidence and skewness conditions in the definition: lines within either set are pairwise skew, and each line meets exactly $d+2$ lines in the other set. A **quadric configuration** on $X$ is the configuration of lines referred to in the source.

**Quadric-configuration conjecture.** Every double $2d$ on $X$ consists of $4d$ lines that are the union of two quadric configurations on $X$.

The preceding theorem establishes existence of double $2d$ configurations on every smooth extremal surface, while this conjecture asserts that all such configurations arise from pairs of quadric configurations. The source provides no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

record.title: An unknown-order-property characterization of quadratic atomicity and binary error
record.statement: Let $\mathrm{XOP}_2$ be a prospective, as-yet-undefined generalization of the order property, and write $\mathrm{NXOP}_2$ for its negation. Let a property be **quadratically atomic** in the group setting and admit **binary $\operatorname{disc}_{2,3}$-error** in the hereditary $3$-uniform-hypergraph setting, using the paper's definitions. **XOP2 conjecture.** There exists a definition of $\mathrm{XOP}_2$ such that: (i) if an epGP $\mathcal{P}$ is $\mathrm{NXOP}_2$, then $\mathcal{P}$ is quadratically atomic; and (ii) if a hereditary property $\mathcal{H}$ of $3$-uniform hypergraphs is $\mathrm{NXOP}_2$, then $\mathcal{H}$ admits binary $\operatorname{disc}_{2,3}$-error. This is presented as an open question motivated by examples that obstruct quadratic atomicity and binary error; no resolution is supplied.

record.title: Nonexistence conjecture for simple sharply 2-transitive groups of finite Morley rank
record.statement:
A group is **sharply 2-transitive** if it acts on a set so that there is a unique group element mapping any ordered pair of distinct points to any other ordered pair of distinct points. A group has **finite Morley rank** when it is a group of finite Morley rank in the sense of model theory. A group is **simple** if it has no nontrivial proper normal subgroups.

**Nonexistence conjecture.** There is no simple sharply 2-transitive group of finite Morley rank.

This conjecture would follow from the conjecture that every sharply 2-transitive group of finite Morley rank is isomorphic to $\mathrm{AGL}_1(K)$ for some algebraically closed field $K$. It is also a particular case of the algebraicity conjecture of Cherlin and Zilber, which states that every infinite simple group of finite Morley rank is an algebraic group over an algebraically closed field; the relevant conjectures remain largely open.
record.source_name: Simon André and Katrin Tent, “Simple sharply 2-transitive groups”, arXiv:2111.09580 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.09580

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2021).

record.title: Explicit formulas conjecture for special symmetric-decomposition polynomials
record.statement:
Let $C_k$ denote the $k$th Catalan number, let $\operatorname{Nar}_{k}(t)$ denote the Narayana polynomial, and define

$$
\overline{\operatorname{Nar}}_{k}^{(j)}(t)=\sum_{i=0}^{k-j}\frac{j+1}{k+1}\binom{k+1}{i}\binom{k+1}{i+j+1}t^{i}.
$$

Let $W_{n,k}^{+}(t)$ and $W_{n,k}^{-}(t)$ be the symmetric-decomposition polynomials. **Special-formula conjecture.** For $k\geq1$,

$$
W_{2k,k}^{+}(t)=(k-1)C_k\operatorname{Nar}_{k-1}(t),\qquad W_{2k,k}^{-}(t)=C_k\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\binom{k-1}{i}^{2}t^i.
$$

For $k\geq2$,

$$
W_{2k,k+1}^{-}(t)=\binom{2k}{k}\operatorname{Nar}_{k-1}(t),\qquad W_{2k,k-1}^{+}(t)=-\frac{t}{2}\binom{2k}{k-2}\overline{\operatorname{Nar}}_{k-2}^{(1)}(t).
$$

These formulas are intended to aid the real-rootedness classification; the source gives no proof and no formulas for the other symmetric-decomposition polynomials.
record.source_name: Miklós Bóna, Stoyan Dimitrov, Gilbert Labelle, Yifei Li, Joseph Pappe, Andrés R. Vindas-Meléndez and Yan Zhuang, “A combinatorial proof of a symmetry for a refinement of the Narayana numbers”, arXiv:2212.10586 (2025).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2021–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2101.02131](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.02131).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.10586

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2022).
